analysis: The PR only changes docs/developer/test.md. It adds a 'Provider authorization guidance' section (head lines 17-28) that documents how to run ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests. The suite covers freshness checks, the receipt-window boundary, disabled rollout, missing or mismatched decisions and exact lease expiry. The text says the tests use fixed snapshots and injected process identity, and that they do not run host probes, change profiles or establish native App Attest acceptance. No code, key handling, endpoint, authorization logic, cache storage or trust-boundary behavior changes. The doc makes no claim of production qualification and does not weaken the TB-011 / T-052 / T-053 / T-057 contracts. It does not alter the T-041 SSD cache posture either. I examined both base text units (lines 1-474 and 475-939). The remainder is unchanged context on provider tests, such as the SSD test temp volume selector, add-on hold tests and the endpoint resumption and logout tests. None of it was modified. I found no concrete security regression and no gap that requires a threat-model update. Not verified: that the named test suite and the production status/doctor freshness code exist and behave as described. That is outside the supplied evidence, but it is a documentation accuracy question, not a security finding.
